name: Ramp
text: Add a single, high-contrast focus ring that appears immediately on keyboard navigation and stays visible. This ensures every interactive element is discoverable without relying on color alone, meeting WCAG 2.2 Level AA for keyboard users. The trade-off is a slight visual clutter for mouse users, but it’s minimal and outweighed by the accessibility win.

name: Reader
text: The always-visible ring creates real fatigue for sighted keyboard users—cognitive noise rises with every tab. Instead, make the ring appear only when the user tabs, then fade after 2 seconds; this keeps discoverability without constant clutter. Test with 5 keyboard-only users: if none report distraction, adopt the fade.

name: Reader
text: The 2-second fade risks missing the user’s next tab—especially on slow machines or long pages—so the ring may vanish mid-navigation. Instead, keep the ring visible until the next tab, then fade only after 1 second of inactivity. Settle it with 5 keyboard-only users: if any lose track of focus, the ring stays visible until the next action.
